name: Icosahedral virus capsids and fivefold rotation
summary: Many sphere-like viruses have protein shells (capsids) with icosahedral symmetry. The primary paper describes cowpea chlorotic mottle virus as having six fivefold rotation axes, ten threefold axes, and fifteen twofold axes. A fivefold symmetry operation corresponds to a 72-degree turn (360/5).
source_title: Origin of icosahedral symmetry in viruses
caveat: Not all viruses have icosahedral capsids; the paper documents exceptions, including HIV. The program compares sampled projected angular gaps with a 72-degree catalog target. An angular coincidence does not establish capsid geometry or a biological cause, and sampled Givens rotations are not an exhaustive grand tour or a capsid reconstruction.
